stories.headline: Entire texture of CM Vijay’s election case changed, says Madras High Court Judge
stories.title: Entire texture of CM Vijay’s election case changed, says Madras High Court Judge
stories.summary: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan wants to know how Mr. Vijay would overcome the Supreme Court rulings on the subject
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The hearing on Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s plea to reject an election petition filed against his victory from the Perambur constituency took an interesting turn on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), with Justice V. Lakshminarayanan of the Madras High Court remarking that the entire texture of the case had changed in view of the Supreme Court judgments cited by counsel for the election petitioner.

After hearing the arguments made on behalf of the Chief Minister on Monday and Tuesday, the Judge began firing a volley of questions at the election petitioner’s counsel on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), asking how some alleged discrepancies in assets worth over ₹600 crore declared by Mr. Vijay would amount to undue influence over voters or could be termed as a corrupt electoral practice.

The Judge wanted to know whether the voters in the Perambur constituency would have been swayed in one direction or the other simply because there was a difference of a few crores or a few lakhs in the assets declared by the Chief Minister, especially in light of the fact that he was a “superstar” in the cinema industry and had voluntarily declared both movable and immovable properties worth more than ₹600 crore.
The Judge said he had relied on a chartered accountant to declare his assets while being elevated to the position of a Judge of the High Court.

Therefore, if Mr. Vijay had also declared his assets through a chartered accountant, how could his election itself be declared null and void for any mistakes made by the auditor in such a declaration, the Judge wondered.

He also questioned the challenge made by a voter, S. Dinesh, through his counsel on record, V.R. Shanmuganathan, to the election of the Chief Minister from Perambur on the ground of improper acceptance of the nomination form by the Returning Officer concerned.
The Judge wanted to know how the Returning Officer could be expected to verify the correctness of the declared assets.

In answering the questions, the election petitioner’s counsel said that the Returning Officer was expected to conduct only a summary inquiry, whereas the charge of false declaration, and whether such declaration was made wilfully and deliberately, could be inquired into only by means of leading evidence during the course of trial in an election petition.
Hence, the election petition should not be rejected at the threshold, he argued.

He said, Justice V. Ramasubramanian (during his stint in the Madras High Court before his retirement as a Supreme Court Judge) had in Krishnamoorthy versus Sivakumar (2009) held that “any incorrect information, wrong information, incomplete information, false information, one-sided information, disinformation, misinformation and non-information would certainly interfere with the free exercise of the electoral right of the voter, inasmuch as his choice of candidate will be influenced greatly by the information so furnished or withheld.”
“The view taken by Justice Ramasubramanian was affirmed by the Supreme Court in 2015.
Therefore, I have made out a cause of action for the trial of the election petition and it should not be rejected in limine,” the counsel said.

stories.headline: Govt rolls out digital system for financial sanctions
stories.title: Govt rolls out digital system for financial sanctions
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 7: The Jammu and Kashmir government has approved the operationalisation of the e-sanction and re-appropriation & surrender modules on the Jammu and Kashmir Budget Estimation, Allocation and Monitoring System (JK BEAMS) to digitise the processing of financial sanctions and budget adjustments across the Union Territory. The Finance Department, through government order no. 310-F of 2026, issued under the Budget Division, said the two modules have been technically completed and will now be implemented across all Administrative Departments, Controlling Officers, Heads of Departments, Drawing and Disbursing Officers (DDOs) and other concerned authorities. The move has been taken in line with the 2026-27 State Annual Scheme for Capital Investment (SASCI) guidelines issued by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, particularly the provisions relating to strengthening public finance IT infrastructure in states. Under the e-sanction module, administrative and financial sanctions will be prepared, processed, approved and issued through a prescribed digital workflow within JK BEAMS. The government has directed that sanctions issued through the system shall be digitally signed by the competent authority through the e-Sanction Module, replacing the need for conventional physical processing wherever the module applies. Similarly, proposals relating to budget re-appropriation and surrender will have to be submitted, examined, processed and approved through the newly introduced re-appropriation & surrender module. The finance department has directed authorities to surrender anticipated savings and reallocate funds through the digital module in a timely manner, in accordance with applicable financial rules and delegated powers. According to the order, the status of sanctions as well as re-appropriation and surrender proposals will be available online to concerned authorities. Digital records of all cases will also be maintained through the modules for monitoring, verification and audit purposes. The finance department said the digital system is aimed at reducing dependence on physical files and manual processing while establishing a streamlined workflow and a proper digital audit trail for government financial transactions. The budget division of the finance department will provide technical support for the rollout and implementation of both modules across Jammu and Kashmir. The order was issued by the Financial Commissioner (Additional Chief Secretary), Finance Department, Shailendra Kumar, IAS.

stories.headline: Oceans connect, not divide nations, PM Modi says, calls for secure maritime order
stories.title: Oceans connect, not divide nations, PM Modi says, calls for secure maritime order
stories.summary: PM Narendra Modi emphasized the importance of maritime connectivity and proposed a ceasefire plan for the Black Sea. His vision promotes cooperation and mutual benefit among nations to ensure maritime security. Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan highlighted the interconnectedness of national security and economic security. He urged for collective action among regions to tackle maritime threats effectively.

stories.headline: Chief Justice to preside over NLSIU convocation weeks after he faced protests
stories.title: Chief Justice to preside over NLSIU convocation weeks after he faced protests
stories.summary: Chief Justice to preside over NLSIU convocation weeks after he faced protests
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: The confirmation follows an August controversy, when 165 outgoing students, 409 students from other batches and 128 alumni opposed CJI Surya Kant's proposed convocation participation.

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant will preside over the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru’s convocation ceremony for the outgoing batch on October 17, the university has confirmed.
The CJI will attend the event as NLSIU Chancellor, while theatre artist Arundhati Nag will be the Chief Guest and deliver the convocation address.
The confirmation comes weeks after a controversy over the proposed participation of the CJI at the university’s convocation.
In August, around 165 students from the outgoing 2026 batch, along with 409 students from other batches and 128 alumni, had opposed CJI Surya Kant being invited as the Chief Guest.

The protest came amid a similar boycott campaign at NALSAR University of Law, where students had opposed the CJI’s participation in its convocation over his comments concerning unemployed youngsters and student protests.
NLSIU students had also objected to the proposed attendance of Bar Council of India Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra at their ceremony.
Against this backdrop, NLSIU announced on August 27 that it was cancelling the convocation, citing “unavoidable circumstances”.
The university, however, revoked its decision last month and decided to proceed with the ceremony, without initially providing explicit confirmation on whether the CJI would attend.
The latest communication settles that uncertainty, confirming Surya Kant’s presence in his capacity as Chancellor.

With Arundhati Nag set to deliver the address, the October 17 ceremony will now bring together the university’s graduating students, faculty and guests following weeks of uncertainty surrounding the event.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Flags Delhi HC Judgment Impeding Speedy Execution Of Civil Decrees
stories.title: Supreme Court Flags Delhi HC Judgment Impeding Speedy Execution Of Civil Decrees
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(October 7) orally said that it will have to do something about a division bench judgment of the Delhi High Court that is apparently coming in the way of the Court in expeditiously disposing of the execution petitions.
At the same time, it expressed some hope considering that in the last six months, a significant number of execution petitions have been disposed off, particularly led by the Gujarat High Court.
A bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran has been hearing a matter concerning the disposal of pending execution petitions across the country.
To recall, on March 6, 2025, the Supreme Court asked the High Courts to collate data on the pendency of 8.8 lac execution petitions across the District Courts nationwide.
It appointed Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan as amicus in this case and set a deadline of six months to dispose of the petitions.
In today's hearing, the amicus referred to his report and pointed out that around 17,000 fresh execution petitions came to be pending before the Delhi High Court in the last six months.

He stated that the reason could be that the division bench of the Delhi High Court in Delhi Chemicals and Pharmaceutical Works Pvt (2021) modified the earlier judgment of Bhandari Engineers, wherein the single judge had set mandatory guidelines for disclosure of assets and income by the judgment-debtor with an aim to dispose of the execution petitions.
On this, Justice Pardiwala asked if the division bench's judgment has been challenged or not.
"Have you placed that division bench judgment or not?
This DB judgment is creating trouble?
This judgment was rendered in a litigation by two private parties and nobody has questioned this judgment so far?

Because of this DB, this 151 [Code of Civil Procedure empowers the Court to make such orders as would be necessary to secure ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the Court] powers are not being exercised.

stories.headline: Airtel hikes postpaid tariffs after over two years, sets the tone for peers
stories.title: Airtel hikes postpaid tariffs after over two years, sets the tone for peers
stories.summary: Airtel’s move comes just weeks ahead of the expected initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms, the parent of Reliance Jio, the market leader by subscribers.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India’s telecom tariff battle is back in play after an over two-year lull in postpaid charge revisions.
Bharti Airtel Ltd has raised prices across postpaid plans by 3-11%, a move that could possibly trigger a fresh round of industry-wide hikes in the chase for higher user spends.

Bharti Airtel, India’s second largest telecom operator by market share, has increased its tariffs by ₹50 across all its postpaid plans, also introducing its added benefit of free international roaming, Fast Lane technology, safety features and entertainment, the company said in a release on Wednesday.
The new tariffs will kick in on 8 October.
Airtel’s move comes just weeks ahead of the expected initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms, the parent of Reliance Jio, the market leader by subscribers.
A tariff increase can lift Airtel's revenues—and, in turn, valuations—putting pressure on Jio to follow suit as it prepares to sell shares to public investors.
For India's telecom industry, hiking tariffs and pushing subscribers up the value chain is the only way to bump up their revenues.
Airtel had last raised its headline tariffs in June 2024, after a gap of two years, following Jio.
The same was driven by the industry’s move to improve return on capital employed and Arpu.
Airtel's postpaid hikes in 2024 were in the 13-20% range.
That year, the tariff hikes were led by Jio, and its private sector peers Airtel and Vodafone Idea took cue.
Airtel currently has six postpaid plans.
